column7: Answers an owner-scoped tasks/get through the route whose delivery check refuses a stored result the caller can no longer reach (withheld target, NoView account), after the account pre-pass ran in the same memo (MIK-8392)
Decides that a caller's principal can never bind a managed account key, so its stored read answers the live call's refusal instead of a retryable error (MIK-8392 D-UB)
Reads the caller's managed-account view without a mint and classifies the failure (no view, unavailable, unjudged) that decides whether a stored read is served, refused or retried (MIK-8392)
Decides whether an account key can be built for a principal under the descriptor; a false answer turns a stored read into the live call's permanent refusal (MIK-8392)
Resolves the caller's current grant mint-free and maps a custody refusal through refusal(): absent, revoked and reconnect-required are no view, everything else is unavailable (MIK-8392)
Fills the account outcomes the delivery check reads, for the owner's own task only; a skipped fill fails closed (retryable), never open (MIK-8392 N0)
Answers the local operator's stdio tasks/get through the route whose delivery check refuses a stored result the caller can no longer reach, after the account pre-pass ran in the same memo (MIK-8392)

Runs the stored-read pre-pass under the request's live policy caller, so a cold claim the policy already refuses is skipped before it resolves (MIK-8392 F4); a wrong caller could only cause an extra resolution, never a delivery
Builds the one policy caller the stored-result delivery check and the stored-read pre-pass judge under; a wrong field would authorize a stored read as another caller (MIK-8392)
Classifies a mint-free managed-account view read, keeping a busy custody apart from no view, so a busy answers retry rather than absent and leaves no no-view marker (MIK-8392 Busy parity)

Recognises only a gateway-sealed transient answer, never a backend look-alike; it gates the nonce refund for a busy call, so a wrong match would give back the nonce of a call that may have run (MIK-8392)
Builds the one sealed retryable answer the live call and the stored read both return, and carries the seal transient_data checks (MIK-8392 Busy parity)

Judges each recorded target's catalogue view for a stored read (withheld, cold, refused) before any output; a wrong arm would deliver a stored result to a caller who can no longer see the tool (MIK-8392)
Judges each recorded target's account outcome from the request memo (no view, busy, unavailable, unfilled) before any output; a wrong arm would deliver a revoked account's stored result (MIK-8392)
Decides a stored read's view of one target's catalogue (shared or the caller's per-user slot, fresh, cold or truncated); a wrong view would judge a withdrawn tool as visible (MIK-8392)
Claims the one attempt to re-establish a caller's cold per-user view under a lease; a wrong claim would let a revoked caller's view be reinstated or many readers resolve at once (MIK-8392)

Classifies a custody failure at the mint: only a busy admission is the typed Busy that answers retryable and refunds the nonce; a wrong arm would refund a nonce after an effect or fold a transient into a permanent refusal (MIK-8428 Case B)

The managed mint (resolve, descriptor fence, refresh, release) with a busy custody kept typed, except at release, after a refresh that may have changed the grant; a wrong mapping refunds a spent nonce (#3892 R7/R8)
Answers a busy mint with the shared sealed retryable error and its one transient idp_refuse at both mint sites; a wrong answer breaks live/stored parity or the audit count (MIK-8428 Case B)
